procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, moderate MDM

documents.title: Follow-up Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Routine recheck. Busy year-end at work, otherwise no new symptoms. Continues in the blinded BP study; their last check was fine per him. Last nephrology visit in the fall, he says no changes were made. Still no notes from that office in our chart.

Meds: lisinopril 20, atorvastatin 40, aspirin 81, plus blinded study medication.
NKDA.

Vitals in flowsheet, BP in his usual range.
Exam: NAD. Heart RRR. Lungs clear. Trace bilateral ankle edema, symmetric, unchanged from prior. No calf tenderness.

A/P
1. HTN: stable, continue current regimen.
2. Membranous nephropathy: CMP, UA today. Asked him to bring or forward his nephrology results.
3. Hyperlipidemia: atorvastatin 40, repeat fasting lipids late spring.
4. Aspirin tolerated.
Return in about 4 months.

documents.title: Results from your visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Hi Patrick, labs look like they did in the fall: kidney function and potassium normal, albumin on the low side and protein in the urine as before. Keep doing what you're doing. Front desk will reach out about a spring appointment.

documents.title: Time to schedule your follow-up
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Hello Mr. Michaud, Dr. asked that we see you about now for a blood pressure visit and fasting labs. Reply here or call the office and we'll find a time that works.

documents.title: RE: Time to schedule your follow-up
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Thanks, it's audit season and I'm swamped. I'll call once things quiet down, probably July.

documents.title: Refill - lisinopril, atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Mail-order request for lisinopril 20 and atorvastatin 40. Last visit 01/07/25; follow-up not yet booked (reminder sent 5/13). Routed.

PCP: 90 days each sent. Please ask him again to schedule; BMP is due.

events.reason: left flank pain and gross hematuria with left leg and scrotal swelling

reports.study: CT abdomen and pelvis with contrast
reports.text: Indication: left flank pain, hematuria, nephrotic syndrome. Technique: CT of the abdomen and pelvis after IV contrast with portal venous and delayed phases. Findings: Occlusive filling defect within the left renal vein consistent with thrombus. Left kidney otherwise unremarkable in size and enhancement; no hydronephrosis. Right kidney normal; right renal vein patent. IVC opacifies normally and is patent. No renal or ureteral stones. Liver, spleen, pancreas and adrenals unremarkable. Bowel normal in caliber. No free fluid. Bladder unremarkable. Bones without acute finding.

documents.title: Emergency department record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
Outside emergency department, date of service 10/14/2025. Received by fax 11/18/2025.

CC: L flank pain, blood in urine, L leg and scrotal swelling.

HPI: 56M with HTN, HLD, nephrotic syndrome, prior MI and stroke, presents with 2 days of L flank pain and grossly bloody urine. Has noticed the L leg and scrotum getting progressively more swollen over the same period. PMH notable for HTN and recent diagnosis of nephrotic syndrome from membranous nephropathy.

PSH: L percutaneous renal biopsy.
Home meds: lisinopril 20 mg daily, atorvastatin 40 mg daily, aspirin 81 mg daily.
Allergies: NKDA.
FHx: father MI 58, mother HTN and DM2, older brother ischemic stroke at 52.
Social: never smoker, social alcohol 1-2/wk, works as a senior financial analyst.

VS: BP 145/90, P 88, afebrile.
Exam: uncomfortable but nontoxic. L lower extremity markedly enlarged vs R with pitting edema up to the mid-thigh. Scrotal edema. Heart regular. Lungs clear.

Data: UA 3+ protein, RBC TNTC. Albumin 2.1. Cr 1.2. D-dimer elevated. Cholesterol 300, LDL 190, HDL 30.
CT A/P with contrast: L renal vein thrombosis.

ED course / MDM: Renal vein thrombosis in the setting of nephrotic syndrome. Heparin started per weight-based protocol. Admitted to medicine.

Dx: Left renal vein thrombosis; nephrotic syndrome.
Disposition: admitted.

procedures.procedure: Hospital discharge day management, 30 minutes or less

documents.title: Discharge summary
documents.author: hospital medicine
documents.body:
Admission 10/14/2025 - discharge 10/17/2025. Received 11/18/2025.

Principal diagnosis: left renal vein thrombosis.
Secondary: nephrotic syndrome due to membranous nephropathy; hypertension; hyperlipidemia.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.

Hospital course: Admitted from the ED after CT showed thrombus in the left renal vein. Treated with IV unfractionated heparin, then transitioned to apixaban. Nephrology consulted while inpatient; nephrotic syndrome is active again and further treatment will be decided in their clinic. Aspirin had been taken for primary prevention only and was stopped now that he is fully anticoagulated. Lisinopril and atorvastatin unchanged. Stable for discharge on hospital day 3.

Discharge medications:
- apixaban 10 mg twice daily through 10/20/2025, then 5 mg twice daily (new)
- lisinopril 20 mg daily (continue)
- atorvastatin 40 mg daily (continue)
- aspirin 81 mg daily - STOP

Follow-up: outpatient nephrology within 1-2 weeks (arranged). Primary care within 2 weeks.
Patient informed his research study team of the admission.

documents.title: Was in the hospital last week
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Hi, wanted you to know I was admitted for a few days last week. Blood clot in the vein of my left kidney, they think from the nephrotic thing flaring. I'm on Eliquis now twice a day and they told me to stop the baby aspirin. Kidney doctor saw me in the hospital and I see her again next week. Can you get the paperwork from the hospital? -Pat

documents.title: RE: Was in the hospital last week
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Patrick, I'm glad you're home and sorry you went through that. We'll request the hospital records today. Please book a visit with me in the next couple of weeks so we can go over everything together and do labs, and bring the discharge papers. Keep taking the apixaban exactly as written and don't miss doses.

documents.title: RE: RE: Was in the hospital last week
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Will do. Nephrology has me coming in a lot right now, I'll call your office once that settles.

documents.title: Hospital records request
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Faxed request to the hospital's HIM department for ED note, imaging, labs and discharge summary, admission 10/14-10/17/25. Release on file from patient.

documents.title: Hospital records - follow-up
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: Nothing back from hospital HIM after 2 weeks. Called; told the first fax was not on file. Sent again with release. Also left patient a voicemail that we still have no post-hospital visit on the schedule.

documents.title: Hospital records received
documents.author: MA
documents.body: Received by fax from the hospital: ED record 10/14/25, CT abdomen/pelvis report, labs, discharge summary 10/17/25 (14 pages). Indexed to the encounter dates and routed to PCP inbox.

documents.title: Refill - lisinopril, atorvastatin
documents.author: MA
documents.body:
Request for lisinopril 20 mg and atorvastatin 40 mg, 90 days. Pharmacy profile also shows apixaban 5 mg BID filled monthly from another prescriber. No office visit since 01/2025. Routed to PCP.

PCP: 90-day supplies sent. He needs a visit before the next refill; please call him.

documents.title: Scheduling a physical
documents.author: patient
documents.body: Sorry for being so slow on this. I'd like to come in for a full physical and catch up on everything since the hospital. Early morning works best, any day after Labor Day.

documents.title: RE: Scheduling a physical
documents.author: front desk
documents.body: You're booked Thursday 9/10 at 7:30 AM for a physical with follow-up from your hospital stay. Please bring your current medication bottles, including anything from nephrology.
